articles.title: ‘KL is klutch’: Delhi Capitals put KL Rahul trade rumours to bed with blunt message
articles.summary: Cricket News: Delhi Capitals have put an end to speculation surrounding KL Rahul’s future, making it clear that the wicketkeeper-batter remains an important part of.
articles.body: Delhi Capitals have put an end to speculation surrounding KL Rahul’s future, making it clear that the wicketkeeper-batter remains an important part of their plans and is not heading to any other franchise.Rumours about a potential trade involving Rahul had gathered momentum on social media over the past two weeks, Neither the franchise nor Rahul had officially addressed the speculation until Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal broke his silence.Jindal made it clear that Delhi have no intention of parting ways with Rahul, highlighting both his performances and his selfless approach to the team.“KL IS KLUTCH FOR @DelhiCapitals - one of the nicest guys I know and one who puts the team before himself always. We have unfinished business and will work hard together to make Delhi proud @IPL,” Jindal wrote on X (formerly Twitter).Rahul responded to Jindal’s post, seemingly putting any doubts over his future to rest.“Thank you, can't wait for the coming season,” the Indian batter wrote.The speculation surrounding Rahul gained traction after Delhi added Rishabh Pant to their squad earlier this year, having traded Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow Super Giants (LSG).The arrival of Pant means Delhi now have two established wicketkeeping options, while both players have experience of leading teams. Axar Patel remains another leadership option, although his position could come under scrutiny following Delhi's disappointing results in the 2025 and 2026 editions.Despite that combination, Jindal's comments suggest Delhi see Rahul as central to their plans rather than someone they are looking to move on.Rahul has also provided the franchise with considerable consistency since joining them. In his first two seasons with Delhi, he crossed the 1,000-run mark, establishing himself as one of their most reliable batters at the top of the order.With Pant expected to take over the wicketkeeping responsibilities, Rahul could now have greater freedom to focus solely on his batting. That could also open the possibility of the two India stars forming an opening partnership for Delhi.The speculation intensified despite the absence of any official indication that a trade was being discussed. Delhi eventually responded to the noise by posting a video with the caption, “Keep the noise coming.”Jindal's latest post, however, has offered a much more direct response.Rahul is coming off a productive 2026 campaign in which he scored 593 runs for Delhi, finishing fourth in the tournament's run-scoring charts. His standout performance came against Shreyas Iyer's Punjab Kings at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, where he smashed an unbeaten 152, the highest individual score by an Indian in the league.Rahul's innings contained nine sixes and came at a strike rate of 226.9, although Delhi's huge total was ultimately chased down by Punjab Kings.For now, though, the message from Delhi is clear: Rahul remains part of their plans, with Jindal insisting that the franchise still has “unfinished business” with the senior batter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Melbourne Renegades first team up for sale as Big Bash opens door for private investment in historic move; what it means
articles.summary: Cricket News: Cricket Australia (CA) has opened the door to private investment in the Big Bash League (BBL), with the Melbourne Renegades set to become the first fr.
articles.body: Cricket Australia (CA) has opened the door to private investment in the Big Bash League (BBL), with the Melbourne Renegades set to become the first franchise offered for sale from the 2027-28 season.The decision comes after months of discussions between Cricket Australia and Australia's state cricket associations over the future of the domestic T20 competition.At a press conference at the SCG on Tuesday afternoon, CA confirmed that the Renegades will be the first BBL franchise to enter the private ownership process. Other BBL and WBBL teams could also be offered for sale in the future under a “self-determination” model.The governing body said the move is aimed at bringing private investment into the T20 competition and strengthening the financial position of Australian cricket as players and teams are increasingly being drawn towards lucrative leagues around the world."CA will invite bids from private owners for the Renegades with a view to them playing the 2027-28 season under new ownership," the governing body said in a statement on Tuesday."Beginning the sales process for the Renegades allows us to take the first step in a self-determination model for our members and represents a defining moment for the game," said Cricket Australia chair Mike Baird."This is a significant decision that has involved an enormous amount of analysis, discussion and collaboration over many months."CA said other franchises could be put on the market at a later stage."Pending the result of that process, CA will consider taking other clubs to market under a self-determination model that gives each state member the ability to assess the optimal pathway for its own club and community."According to cricket.com.au, Hobart Hurricanes, Perth Scorchers and Melbourne Stars are among the other clubs believed to be interested in private investment.The Renegades are owned by Cricket Victoria, which supported CA's original plan. They won the BBL title in the 2018-19 season.The move comes as CA looks to strengthen its finances. Despite a boost in revenue from hosting a five-Test series against India, the game's biggest financial market, CA reported a net deficit of A$11.3 million for the 2024-25 financial year."By opening the door to private investment in the Big Bash Leagues, Cricket Australia is taking a deliberate step to strengthen and secure the long-term future of the game," CA Chairman Mike Baird said in Tuesday's statement.Australia Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced in July that December's BBL 2026-27 season opener between the Renegades and Perth Scorchers would take place in the Chennai.While CA is allowing private ownership, it will continue to control key areas of the competition. Baird said the governing body will retain control over international scheduling, player availability, salary caps and media rights.CA will also have the power to approve or veto investors and set a reserve price for the sale.Any changes to a club's name, colours or branding will also require approval. For the Melbourne Renegades, CA will be the approving authority, while the relevant state body will have that role for the other teams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asia Cup impact: Deepti Sharma moves up to sixth position; Sree Charani retains T20I no. 1 ranking
articles.summary: Cricket News: India continue to make their presence felt at the top of the Women’s T20I bowling rankings, with Sree Charani holding on to the No. 1 spot and Deepti .
articles.body: India continue to make their presence felt at the top of the Women’s T20I bowling rankings, with Sree Charani holding on to the No. 1 spot and Deepti Sharma making a two-place jump to sixth following her strong showing at the Asia Cup 2026.Deepti has been one of India’s standout performers in the tournament, claiming eight wickets in three matches as the team booked its place in the semi-finals.Deepti closes in on CharaniThe right-arm spinner’s consistent performances have earned her a significant rise in the latest rankings. Deepti, who had previously reached the top spot in December last year, is now within 60 rating points of Charani. Sophie Ecclestone, Charlie Dean, Nonkululeko Mlaba and Lauren Bell are the four bowlers positioned between the two Indian stars.With Charani and Deepti occupying the top two positions, India continues to dominate the upper reaches of the T20I bowling rankings.Marufa Akter among big moversSeveral players also made significant gains in the latest T20I rankings after their performances at the Asia Cup. Bangladesh’s Marufa Akter was among the biggest movers, climbing 19 places to 18th in the bowling rankings. Chamari Athapaththu moved up five spots to 28th, while Sultana Khatun gained nine places to share 37th.Thailand’s Thipatcha Putthawong rose four places to 47th, while teammate Suleeporn Laomi jumped 10 spots to 53rd. There were also gains among Bangladesh’s batters, with Sobhana Mostary moving up three places to 36th and Dilara Akter climbing five spots to 62nd.Charlie Dean gains in ODI rankingsThe latest ODI rankings also saw notable movement following England’s home series against Ireland. Stand-in England captain Charlie Dean moved up one place to jointly occupy ninth in the ODI all-rounders’ rankings. She also climbed two spots to share 11th among ODI bowlers after taking three wickets in the three-match series.England’s Lauren Filer made an impressive 14-place jump to 39th, while Ireland’s Cara Murray rose 16 places to 50th in the ODI bowling rankings.Ireland youngster Amy Hunter emerged as the biggest winner among ODI batters, moving up nine places to 11th. England’s Maia Bouchier climbed 13 spots to 42nd, while Sophia Dunkley made an even bigger leap of 26 places to reach 43rd.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Phones confiscated, players sent home: Pakistan's England tour turmoil revives memories of Mohammad Amir, Salman Butt and Mohammad Asif's 2010 Lord's spot-fixing scandal
articles.summary: Cricket News: England has not often been a happy place for Pakistan cricket in recent times. In the ongoing three-Test series, Pakistan have already lost the first .
articles.body: England has not often been a happy place for Pakistan cricket in recent times. In the ongoing three-Test series, Pakistan have already lost the first two matches by big margins. They suffered an innings defeat in the series opener at Headingley before losing the second Test at Lord's by 194 runs. The third Test is set to begin at Edgbaston on Wednesday.However, what followed the defeat at Lord's surprised even those familiar with the unpredictable nature of Pakistan cricket.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sent seven players home and called up another seven, with five of the replacements uncapped at Test level.The PCB also removed Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. They were replaced by Pakistan's white-ball coaches Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke.Salman Ali Agha, who captained Pakistan at Headingley in the absence of the injured Babar Azam, was among those sent home. Left-arm spinner Ali Usman, who took a five-wicket haul in that Test, was also released.Experienced wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan and opener Imam-ul-Haq were also told to leave. Imam did not bat in either innings at Lord's because of a calf injury.Hesson admitted last week that the changes had added to the uncertainty around the team."The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. I don't think anyone wants this to happen in the middle of a series."The situation took another turn on Monday when the PCB announced an investigation into the squad's conduct during the England tour, bringing the issue of match-fixing back into focus.As reported by TimesofIndia.com, the changes within Pakistan cricket were driven by reasons that were “more than cricket” and were not simply a response to the team's poor performances.According to Pakistani outlet 365 News, the players' devices have been handed over to the PCB and will remain in the board's custody until the final Test is completed. The report did not reveal which players had their phones taken, while the PCB has not publicly explained why the devices were confiscated.Horror of 2010The developments have also brought back memories of Pakistan's 2010 spot-fixing scandal, one of the biggest corruption cases in cricket.The scandal took place during Pakistan's tour of England, during the fourth Test at Lord's. It centred on allegations that Pakistani players had deliberately bowled no-balls at specific points in the match in return for money.When Mohammad Amir overstepped the crease while bowling a no-ball against England on the opening day of the 2010 Lord's Test, there was no indication that the moment would become part of a fixing scandal that would affect Pakistan cricket for years.Two days later, it emerged that three no-balls — two by Amir and one by his pace partner Mohammad Asif — were part of a betting deal.Pakistan captain Salman Butt had arranged the deliberate no-balls in return for money offered by undercover journalist Mazhar Majeed, who was posing as a bookmaker.The scandal, exposed in the sting by Britain's now-defunct News of the World tabloid, rocked the cricketing world , and aftershocks can still be felt more than a decade on in Pakistan. Not only did that dark morning at the revered 'home of cricket' derail the careers of three players who were banned and jailed, the saga also led to calls for Pakistan to be booted from international cricket. Butt, Amir and Asif were tried in a London court for offences under the Gambling Act and were jailed in November 2011.Announcing the sentences, the judge underscored the severity of the crime. “The image and integrity of what was once a game, but is now a business, is damaged in the eyes of all, including the many youngsters who regarded three of you as heroes,” Justice Jeremy Cooke said. It marked a new low for Pakistan cricket, already reeling from the aftermath of terror attacks in Lahore on the Sri Lankan team a year before, which triggered the suspension of home internationals.In November 2011, after a high-profile trial in London, all three players were found guilty of corruption and conspiracy to accept illegal payments. Salman Butt received a 30-month prison sentence, Mohammad Asif was jailed for a year, and Mohammad Amir, due to his age and early confession, was sentenced to six months.Only one of them, Amir, returned to international cricket after serving the ICC-ban when he made his comeback in 2016.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s sharp cricket brain shines! 15-year-old plots two big wickets in Duleep Trophy final – Watch
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation is already showing the tactical awareness of a seasoned cricketer. The East .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation is already showing the tactical awareness of a seasoned cricketer. The East Zone vice-captain played a key role in two crucial dismissals as his side tightened the screws on South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.After East Zone piled up a mammoth 708, largely courtesy of captain Ishan Kishan’s magnificent 270, South Zone appeared to be settling into their reply. But Sooryavanshi’s sharp reading of the game helped East Zone strike twice before tea on Day 3.Sooryavanshi trusts his instinct for crucial DRS callThe first breakthrough came when Ricky Bhui appeared to have survived a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar. The pacer zipped one down the leg side as Bhui attempted to guide it away, but the on-field umpire remained unmoved despite the appeal.Sooryavanshi, however, was convinced there was something behind it. The teenager urged Kishan to take the Decision Review System (DRS), and his instinct proved spot on.UltraEdge showed a spike as the ball passed the bat, with wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra completing the catch to send Bhui back.BCCI also highlighted Sooryavanshi’s intervention on social media.“Take it... take it. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi urges the captain to take the review, and it turns out to be successful,” BCCI wrote, while sharing the video of the dismissal on X.It was another example of the youngster’s growing influence in senior cricket. His ability to make the call under pressure was particularly impressive.Teenage vice-captain brings Shami back at the perfect timeSooryavanshi’s tactical contribution did not end with the DRS call.With South Zone at 174/4 and only minutes remaining before tea, the youngster was temporarily standing in as captain after Kishan went off the field. He decided to bring Mohammed Shami back for a short burst despite the veteran pacer having already bowled a demanding spell.Shami had earlier walked off after bowling seven overs and had bowled only twice after lunch. He had also required treatment to his neck from the physio.Yet Sooryavanshi recognised the opportunity to use the experienced seamer for a quick spell before the interval.The move paid immediate dividends.Shami dismissed Smaran Ravichandran, the highest run-scorer of the previous Ranji Trophy season, when the Karnataka batter chased a delivery outside off and nicked it behind. The on-field umpire again did not give the batter out, but this time Kushagra urged Sooryavanshi to review.UltraEdge once again confirmed the edge.Ravichandran was gone, South Zone were reduced to 176/5, and Sooryavanshi had played a direct role in two of East Zone’s most important wickets.DRS instinct becoming a Sooryavanshi trademarkThe decision-making has not been a one-off for Sooryavanshi in this Duleep Trophy campaign.During East Zone’s semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru, the youngster made another bold DRS call after Aryan Juyal was initially given not out following a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar.Juyal, batting on 46, pushed hard at a delivery outside off and the East Zone players immediately appealed. When the umpire rejected the appeal, there was some hesitation among the fielders over whether to review.Sooryavanshi trusted his instinct and called for the review at the last moment. UltraEdge detected a spike, confirming the edge and handing East Zone a crucial wicket.The youngster had also spoken about his willingness to contribute with the ball during the tournament, joking that he considered himself a “wicket-taker”.“Opponent team's wickets weren't falling, so I was asked to bowl two or three overs. Ishan Bhaiya felt like he was taking a risk, but he didn't know that I am a wicket-taker,” Sooryavanshi said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic.His batting may have made him one of Indian cricket’s most talked-about teenage prospects, but his Duleep Trophy campaign is increasingly showcasing another side of his game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
